title: Unidas Talamanca women’s safety march from Puerto Viejo to Playa Cocles
location: Puerto Viejo to Playa Cocles, Limón
participants_original: S004: turnout described as among the collective’s best, without a number; S005: “a group of women,” without a number.
threshold_50_evidence: The reviewed source gives no numeric turnout estimate; the 50-person threshold is unestablished.

start_date.summary: Both articles say the march occurred “this Thursday”; S004 is dated 13 January and S005 is dated 14 January, identifying the action date as 13 January.

location.summary: S004 gives a route from Puerto Viejo to Playa Cocles; S005 says streets of Puerto Viejo.

organizer.summary: Both reports identify Unidas Talamanca as the organizer/caller.

demands.summary: S005 reports a demand for greater protection for women; S004 quotes a call for police to believe women, while describing the march’s immediate audience as the local public.

participants_original.summary: S004 says turnout was among the collective’s best without giving a number; S005 says a group of women, without a numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither report quantifies turnout; the qualitative phrase “among the collective’s best” does not establish 50 participants.

state_response.accommodation.summary: S004 reports an announced urgent intervention and planned police training without implementation or direct causal linkage. S005 reports a police-post project statement made before the march. No post-march qualifying accommodation is established.

notes: S004 and S005 are separate outlet reports of one march on Thursday 13 January, not two events. S004 gives the route and reports a spokesperson’s call for police to believe women; S005 says the collective demanded greater protection after a 6 January sexual assault. S004 says the action sought to make the town hear women more than to appeal to authorities, so the domestic state/policy target is supported by the stated demand about police but merits review. Planned intervention/training and a pre-march police-post statement are not coded as a response caused by this march. The UCR chronology’s 7 and 14 January entries remain unresolved relative to this event.
open_questions: Was turnout at least 50? S004’s “among the collective’s best” has no numeric basis.
Is this distinct from UCR’s 7 January Puerto Viejo entry and/or the chronology’s 14 January entry?
What was the physical end date?
Were any announced official measures implemented as a response to this march?
